messages.content: Show my risk score and attack surface

Your overall risk score is 72/100 — moderate risk. Top exposures: 9 users have excessive permissions in your Finance AD Group, 2 admin accounts are inactive (45+ days dormant), and 4 group memberships in Exchange admin are stale. Want me to break any of these down?
Tell me about the Finance group exposures

The Finance AD Group has 9 users with Read/Write/Modify permissions on payroll data. Of those, 2 are contractors, 1 is a service account, and 3 haven't accessed the data in 60+ days. The biggest concern is that contractor access is still active 30 days after their engagement ended.
What action should I take first?
Who has access to sensitive data?
247 users have direct or inherited access to data tagged 'sensitive' — that includes PII, financial records, and HR files. 38 of them haven't logged in in 30+ days. Want a breakdown by data type?
Yes, focus on PII
Audit AD changes from this week

184 changes detected in the last 7 days. Notable: 14 new accounts created, 6 admin permissions granted, 3 group policy modifications, and 2 schema changes. The schema changes are flagged as high-risk.
What schema changes?

On Monday at 02:14 AM, the schema was modified by user 'svc-replication'. The change added a new attribute to the User class. The timing (after-hours) and the service account origin make this worth investigating.
Could it be a Golden Ticket attack?

Possible. The combination of after-hours timing + schema modification + service account is consistent with reconnaissance for a Golden Ticket or DCSync attack. I'd recommend rotating the krbtgt password and reviewing all changes by 'svc-replication' in the last 48 hours.
Generate me a report
Show users with admin rights I should review
17 users have admin or admin-equivalent privileges in your environment. 4 are Domain Admins, 6 are Enterprise Admins, and 7 have admin-level access to specific systems.
Filter to those who haven't used admin rights in 30 days

8 of the 17 admins haven't used their elevated privileges in the last 30 days. 3 haven't used them in 90+ days, including 'admin-jdoe' (last admin action: 127 days ago) and 'svc-backup-admin' (last admin action: 184 days ago).
Show me admin-jdoe

admin-jdoe is John Doe in IT Operations. He has Domain Admin, Local Admin on 23 servers, and root access to 2 Linux hosts. Last admin action was 127 days ago when he reset a password. Last interactive login: 12 days ago (not as admin).
What's your recommendation?
Recommend: 1) Move John to a Just-In-Time admin model for routine tasks, 2) Remove standing Domain Admin if not needed for current role, 3) Audit svc-backup-admin — likely needs to be deactivated.
Generate the report
Am I ready for Copilot?

Your Copilot readiness score is 62/100 — not yet recommended for full rollout. Top blockers: 47 users have access to sensitive data they shouldn't, 12% of your shared files have no sensitivity labels, and DLP policies don't yet cover M365 Copilot inputs.
What should I fix first?

Fix in this order: 1) Remediate the 47 over-permissioned users (high impact, 1-2 day effort), 2) Auto-classify the unlabeled files using Sensitivity Labels with auto-apply (1 day), 3) Extend DLP policies to Copilot via Microsoft Purview (4 hours). After these, your readiness should be ~85+.
How do I generate a CCPA report?
I can generate it for you. CCPA reporting in Lepide covers: access logs for personal data, data deletion records, and consent tracking. Should I run it for the last 90 days?
Yes, last 90 days

Generated. The report covers 1,247 CCPA-relevant events. 14 are access requests, 3 are deletion requests, and 1,230 are routine access logs to PII. All deletion requests were fulfilled within the 45-day window. Want me to email it?
Email it to compliance@
Sent to compliance@yourcompany.com. The report ID is CCPA-2026-Q1-0042 and is also saved to your My Lepide dashboard.

actions.label: Create a summary for the board

Who has access to sensitive data?.content: Great question — this is one of those things that tends to creep up over time. I scanned everything and found some stuff you'll want to know about.
Who has access to sensitive data?.finding: You've got 33,742 sensitive files across your systems. The concerning part? 847 of them are over-exposed, meaning more people can access them than should be able to.
Who has access to sensitive data?.why: The biggest issue is in Finance Shares — 9 people there have way more access than their job requires. Also spotted PII sitting in 3 public-facing OneDrive folders, which is a GDPR and HIPAA headache waiting to happen.
Who has access to sensitive data?.affected: SharePoint has the most files (2.1M), but File Shares have the highest sensitive percentage (18%). SQL Server only has 320K files but 22% of them are sensitive — that's worth watching.
Who has access to sensitive data?.nextStep: I'd say let's tackle those 847 over-exposed files first. I can show you exactly which ones they are and who shouldn't have access. We could also set up automatic cleanup policies for the easy ones.

Audit AD changes from this week.content: Quite a busy week in Active Directory, actually! Let me walk you through the highlights — there are a few things I think you should see.
Audit AD changes from this week.finding: 47 changes across 12 AD groups this week. Three of those were bulk operations that affected 9+ users each. That's unusually high for your environment.
Audit AD changes from this week.why: Here's the one that caught my eye — on Tuesday, someone did a direct group-level permission grant in the Finance AD Group that completely skipped your approval workflow. Could be legit, could be someone taking a shortcut. Either way, it needs a look.
Audit AD changes from this week.affected: Finance AD Group got 9 new members, Exchange Admin Group got 4, and there were 5 individual role changes scattered across other groups
Audit AD changes from this week.nextStep: That unapproved change is the priority. If it was intentional, we just need to document it. If not, we should roll it back before it becomes a bigger issue. Want me to pull up the details?

Generate a compliance status report.content: On it! I've got your compliance data right here. The good news is you're mostly in good shape — 82% overall. But there are a few gaps we should talk about before your next audit.
Generate a compliance status report.finding: Three control failures are still open, and one of them — AC-2.3 — has zero evidence of review. That's the one that'll get flagged first if an auditor comes knocking.
Generate a compliance status report.why: The missing review on AC-2.3 creates what auditors call a "traceability gap." Basically, there's no paper trail showing someone actually looked at it. The underlying data exists in Lepide, though — so fixing this is mostly about documenting the review.
Generate a compliance status report.affected: SOX 404, NIST AC-2, and ISO 27001 A.9 are all affected by this one control failure. Plus there are 12 exceptions across other control families that need attention.
Generate a compliance status report.nextStep: I've already pre-filled a report template with this week's data. You can tweak it, add your own notes, and export it as a PDF. Should I open it up for you?

actions.label: Let me see those control failures

Find stale privileged accounts.content: Oh yeah, this is one of my favorite things to check because it's such a quick win. Let me look... yep, found some.
Find stale privileged accounts.finding: 14 accounts with admin-level access haven't logged in for over 30 days. Two of them are particularly concerning — they've been dormant for 45+ days and still have Domain Admin access.
Find stale privileged accounts.why: These are basically unlocked doors that nobody's using. If an attacker compromises one of these, they get full admin access without triggering any of the usual login alerts. It's one of the easiest attack vectors to exploit.
Find stale privileged accounts.affected: j.smith@corp.com hasn't logged in for 47 days (Finance Admin), m.jones@corp.com for 62 days (DevOps Admin). The other 12 are between 30-45 days inactive.
Find stale privileged accounts.nextStep: The fastest fix? Revoke access for those top two right now — it's completely reversible within 30 days if someone complains. For the rest, let's set up a watchlist so we're alerted if any more go stale. Sound good?

What can Lepide AI help me audit?.why: Right now your setup is partial — Entra ID is connected but AD isn't yet. Once we get AD plugged in, I'll be able to see about 70% more of what's happening in your environment. That's when things get really useful.

How does Lepide detect insider threats?.content: Great question! I use three layers of detection, and each one catches different types of threats. Let me break it down simply.
How does Lepide detect insider threats?.finding: Layer 1: Rule-based alerts (like "admin rights granted outside business hours"). Layer 2: Behavioral baselines (I learn what's normal for each user and flag deviations). Layer 3: AI correlation (I connect multiple low-risk events that together might indicate something bigger).
How does Lepide detect insider threats?.why: Most security tools only do Layer 1 — basic rules. But attackers know those rules too. My behavioral analysis (Layer 2) catches the stuff rules miss because I know what "normal" looks like for each user. And the AI layer? That's where I catch the really sneaky stuff.
How does Lepide detect insider threats?.affected: I watch: AD changes, file access patterns, permission modifications, login anomalies, data movement, Group Policy changes, and Copilot interactions
How does Lepide detect insider threats?.nextStep: Once your environment is fully connected, I'll spend about 7-14 days learning everyone's patterns. After that, I start catching anomalies automatically. The more sources you connect, the smarter I get.

What reports can I generate?.finding: Main report types: Executive Risk Summary, Compliance Status (per framework), Permission Analysis, Data Classification, Change Audit Trail, User Activity, Stale Account Report, and fully custom reports based on whatever you ask me.
What reports can I generate?.why: Every report pulls live data from your connected sources — no stale information. You can schedule them daily, weekly, or monthly so they just show up without you having to think about it. PDFs for formal stuff, CSVs for data crunching.
What reports can I generate?.affected: Available frameworks: SOX, NIST, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001 · Formats: PDF, CSV · Delivery: on-demand, scheduled, email
What reports can I generate?.nextStep: Want to try one? I can generate a sample report from your Entra ID data right now so you can see what the full thing would look like once everything's connected.
